topic: Lead intake and first-reply drafting for an events business
summary: AI-assisted inquiry organization and response drafting may reduce repetitive intake work while keeping staff approval before messages are sent.

findings.text: First replies to new inquiries are still written by hand.
findings.reason: The business description and a published small-business sales guide both describe manual first contact.

findings.text: A person should approve a message before it is sent.
findings.reason: Published business guidance treats outbound commercial messages as something the business remains responsible for.

findings.text: Keeping inquiry details in one place makes the first reply easier to draft.
findings.reason: A public customer-service guide describes collecting the request before writing a response.

findings.text: A reliable hours-saved percentage for event businesses was not established.
findings.reason: The reviewed sources do not measure this exact workflow.

recommendations.text: Organize each inquiry and prepare a first reply for staff to approve before anything is sent.

sources.title: AI risk management framework
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology

sources.title: Keep your AI claims in check

evidence.excerpt: Small businesses are told to respond to customer inquiries as part of selling, which still leaves the wording of that first reply to the business.
Businesses remain responsible for the marketing messages they send.
Serving customers starts with understanding what they asked for before a response goes out.
General AI guidance does not publish a time-saved figure for event-business inquiry replies.

evidence_gaps.text: No reliable benchmark was found for this exact type of business.
No source establishes a guaranteed time-saving percentage.

limitations: This fixture is synthetic development data shaped like a future NVR Labs result. It is not a live research run.
